edges.description: SLC38A8 is required for foveal development independently of melanin; the steps between loss of SNAT8 and failed foveal specialisation are not known.
Loss of Slc38a8 reduces the uncrossed (ipsilateral) retinal projection in mice; how SNAT8 influences axon routing is not known.

nodes.description: Primary visual cortex receives input from the contralateral eye only, and each cortical location represents mirror-symmetric points in both visual hemifields.

evidence.reference_title: Altered organization of the visual cortex in FHONDA syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Each cortical location was found to contain a pRF in each visual hemifeld and opposing hemifields were represented as retinotopic cortical overlays of mirror-symmetrical locations across the vertical meridian.

nodes.description: Retinal development arrests at an early stage: the foveal pit does not form, inner retinal layers remain continuous across the fovea and cone outer segments do not lengthen, implying low foveal cone density. The arrest is more severe than the graded foveal hypoplasia of albinism or PAX6 disease and is not progressive.

evidence.reference_title: SLC38A8 mutations result in arrested retinal development with loss of cone photoreceptor specialization.
evidence.snippet: All patients had severe grades of arrested retinal development with lack of a foveal pit and no cone photoreceptor outer segment lengthening.

evidence.reference_title: SLC38A8 mutations result in arrested retinal development with loss of cone photoreceptor specialization.
evidence.snippet: Unlike other disorders (such as albinism or PAX6 mutations) which exhibit a spectrum of foveal hypoplasia, SLC38A8 mutations have arrest of retinal development at an earlier stage resulting in a more under-developed retina and severe phenotype.

nodes.description: Infantile nystagmus in all reported patients; jerk waveforms are most common, with pendular and periodic alternating forms also described.

evidence.reference_title: Novel Biallelic Variants and Phenotypic Features in Patients with SLC38A8-Related Foveal Hypoplasia.
evidence.snippet: Of the 58 affected individuals in 37 families, 100% (n = 58) had foveal hypoplasia and nystagmus, while 97% (29 out of the 30 who underwent VEP testing) showed chiasmal misrouting.

evidence.snippet: Compared to albinism, the FHONDA syndrome appears to have a more narrow phenotypic spectrum, consisting of nonprogressive moderately to severely reduced VA, nystagmus, severe foveal hypoplasia, and misrouting.

evidence.reference_title: Altered organization of the visual cortex in FHONDA syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We determined the cortical organization in a novel congenital visual pathway disorder, FHONDA-syndrome, where the axons from the temporal retina abnormally cross to the contralateral hemisphere.

evidence.reference_title: The Phenotypic and Mutational Spectrum of the FHONDA Syndrome and Oculocutaneous Albinism: Similarities and Differences.
evidence.snippet: Misrouting was present in all nine tested patients. None of the patients had any signs of hypopigmentation of skin and hair.

evidence.reference_title: Recessive mutations in SLC38A8 cause foveal hypoplasia and optic nerve misrouting without albinism.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report that these defects can occur independently of albinism in people with recessive mutations in the putative glutamine transporter gene SLC38A8. Nine different mutations were identified in seven Asian and European families.

evidence.reference_title: Isolated foveal hypoplasia with secondary nystagmus and low vision is associated with a homozygous SLC38A8 mutation.
evidence.snippet: Whole-exome sequencing identified a single missense mutation in the homozygosity region: c.95T>G, p.(Ile32Ser), in a conserved amino acid within the first predicted transmembrane domain of SLC38A8. The mutation fully segregated with the disease-associated phenotype

evidence.reference_title: SLC38A8 mutations result in arrested retinal development with loss of cone photoreceptor specialization.
evidence.snippet: We report 16 novel SLC38A8 mutations. The sixth transmembrane domain is most frequently disrupted by missense SLC38A8 mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the mutational and phenotypical spectrum of FHONDA syndrome.
evidence.snippet: FHONDA is associated with biallelic disease-causing variants in the SLC38A8 gene, which has a strong expression in the photoreceptor layer. To date, 60 different disease-causing variants in the SLC38A8 gene have been described.

nodes.description: Biallelic SLC38A8 variants are expected to abolish or reduce SNAT8, a sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporter whose substrates include L-glutamine, L-alanine, L-arginine, L-histidine and L-aspartate. Truncating and canonical splice variants are predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay, and missense variants are predicted to destabilise the protein. Transport by patient variants has not been measured in the sources cited here, so loss of transport is inferred rather than demonstrated.

evidence.reference_title: Transport of L-glutamine, L-alanine, L-arginine and L-histidine by the neuron-specific Slc38a8 (SNAT8) in CNS.
evidence.snippet: We show that SLC38A8 has preference for transporting L-glutamine, L-alanine, L-arginine, L-histidine and L-aspartate using a Na+-dependent transport mechanism and that the functional characteristics of SNAT8 have highest similarity to the known System A transporters.

evidence.reference_title: SLC38A8 mutations result in arrested retinal development with loss of cone photoreceptor specialization.
evidence.snippet: SLC38A8 is a putative glutamine transporter with strong expression within the photoreceptor layer in the retina.

evidence.reference_title: SLC38A8 mutations result in arrested retinal development with loss of cone photoreceptor specialization.
evidence.snippet: All amino acid substitutions are predicted to be destabilizing (Fig. 2).

evidence.reference_title: Structural modeling of a novel SLC38A8 mutation that causes foveal hypoplasia.
evidence.snippet: Our modeling also predicted that the mutation destabilizes the protein by altering the electrostatic potential within the channel pore.

nodes.description: CRISPR/Cas9 allele truncating Slc38a8 at p.Pro196*, equivalent to human p.Pro199* and close to the patient allele p.Gln200*. Mice have wild-type eye and coat pigmentation, a reduced ipsilateral retinal projection, reduced scotopic ERG response, reduced optomotor visual acuity and subcellular abnormalities of the retinal pigment epithelium.
SLC38A8 c.95T>G, p.(Ile32Ser), in the first predicted transmembrane domain; recurrent in Israeli families of Jewish Indian (Mumbai) and Karaite Jewish origin.

evidence.reference_title: The pathogenicity of SLC38A8 in five families with foveal hypoplasia and congenital nystagmus.
evidence.snippet: Molecular analysis revealed a recently described homozygous mutation, c.95T > G; p.Ile32Ser, in two families of Jewish Indian descent, and the same mutation in two families of Karaite Jewish descent.
